comparison_block.heading: Markets.com vs IG — Which Is Better in 2026?
comparison_block.body: Both are FCA + CySEC + ASIC regulated brokers with institutional parents, spread betting for UK clients, and massive instrument ranges. IG wins on pricing transparency (published spreads from 0.6 pips), platform depth (ProRealTime, L2 Dealer), instrument count (17,000+), and educational resources. Markets.com wins on simplicity — zero commission, zero deposit/withdrawal fees, and a cleaner onboarding experience for traders who want straightforward CFD access without complexity. For the active trader who values tight spreads and advanced tools, IG. For the intermediate trader who values simplicity and zero-fee transactions, Markets.com.

sections.heading: Is Markets.com Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Markets.com is owned by Finalto Limited, which is a subsidiary of Playtech PLC — a company listed on the London Stock Exchange with a market capitalisation exceeding GBP 3 billion. That is not a random offshore entity. That is a publicly traded corporation filing annual reports with the LSE, audited by Big Four accounting firms, and answerable to institutional shareholders. The regulatory coverage matches: FCA in the UK, CySEC in Cyprus, ASIC in Australia — three Tier-1 regulators covering the jurisdictions that matter most to retail traders.

The trading proposition is straightforward: 2,200+ CFDs across every major asset class, zero commission, zero deposit fees, zero withdrawal fees. You pay the spread and nothing else. That simplicity is genuinely appealing. No hidden charges, no confusing commission structures, no surprise fees on your statement. What you see is what you pay.

But simplicity has a cost. The 85.4% retail loss rate — published per FCA and CySEC requirements — is among the highest in the industry. When a broker earns its revenue exclusively from spreads and client losses on those spreads, an 85.4% loss rate means the model is working extremely well for the broker. The spreads are competitive but not market-leading. You will not get raw ECN pricing here. You will not get 0.0-pip spreads with a commission. If you trade high volume, you are paying more per lot than you would at a dedicated ECN broker. Markets.com trades on convenience and safety, not on being the cheapest option available.

sections.heading: Is Markets.com Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Five regulatory licences across four jurisdictions — three of which are Tier-1. Safecap Investments Ltd operates under CySEC licence 092/08, the original regulatory home since 2008. Markets.com (UK) operates under FCA authorisation 607305 with FSCS coverage up to GBP 85,000 for eligible clients. Markets.com Australia operates under ASIC licence 424008 — segregated client funds but no compensation scheme. Markets.com South Africa operates under FSCA licence 46860. The offshore entity operates under BVI FSC licence SIBA/L/14/1067 for clients outside regulated jurisdictions.

The institutional backing is what separates Markets.com from most competitors. Finalto Limited — the direct parent — is a major institutional liquidity and technology provider serving banks and brokers globally. Finalto itself is owned by Playtech PLC (LON: PTEC), a FTSE 250 company with annual revenues exceeding EUR 1.7 billion. This means Markets.com has access to institutional-grade liquidity infrastructure and operates within a corporate governance framework that most retail brokers simply cannot match.

No regulatory fines, sanctions, or enforcement actions against Markets.com appear in public records. No FCA clone warnings. No CySEC sanctions. Clean regulatory record across all five jurisdictions. NAFT last verified Markets.com regulation in May 2026.

sections.heading: Markets.com Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
The pricing model is spread-only with zero commission on all CFD instruments. No commission on forex. No commission on indices. No commission on commodities. No commission on shares CFDs. Every cost is embedded in the spread — which makes pricing simple to understand but harder to compare against commission-based brokers.

Typical EUR/USD spreads run from 1.2 pips during London/New York sessions — translating to approximately $12 per standard lot all-in. That is higher than ECN brokers like IC Markets (0.0 + $7 commission = $7 per lot) or Pepperstone Razor (0.0 + $7 = $7 per lot). But it is competitive against other spread-only brokers and eliminates the need to calculate commission costs separately.

Four account types serve different needs. The Classic Account is the standard offering for most traders. Spread Betting is available exclusively for UK residents — profits are tax-free under current HMRC rules, which is a genuine financial advantage. The Islamic Account removes swap charges for Sharia compliance. Corporate Accounts are available for companies and funds.

The zero-fee structure on deposits and withdrawals is genuinely differentiating. No deposit fee. No withdrawal fee. No inactivity fee published. No currency conversion fee on major deposit currencies. This removes the friction that catches traders at other brokers — particularly the hidden conversion charges that platforms like eToro impose.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Markets.com?
sections.body:
Deposits are instant via card, Skrill, Neteller, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. Wire transfers take 2-5 business days. Minimum deposit is $100/€100/£100 across all methods — straightforward and consistent. No deposit fees on any method.

Withdrawals process within 1-3 business days with zero fees. No withdrawal charge on any method — a genuine competitive advantage when brokers like eToro charge $5 per withdrawal and others impose percentage-based fees. Minimum withdrawal aligns with method minimums.

The absence of fees on both sides of the transaction is Markets.com's strongest operational feature. You deposit without cost, trade at the spread, and withdraw without cost. The only cost in the entire lifecycle is the spread itself. This clean structure means you always know exactly what you are paying — no surprise charges on your bank statement, no hidden conversion markups, no monthly maintenance fees eating into dormant balances.

sections.heading: Markets.com Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Markets.com maintains a solid withdrawal reputation with no systematic complaint patterns visible across major review platforms. The broker processes withdrawals within 1-3 business days for most methods, and the zero-fee structure means there are no financial barriers to withdrawal.

Trustpilot presence is moderate — not as heavily reviewed as IG or eToro given the smaller retail footprint. Trust scores from independent review aggregators place Markets.com at 98/100 (FXLeaders), reflecting the combination of Tier-1 regulation, clean record, and institutional backing. The absence of withdrawal complaints at scale is itself a positive signal — when brokers have withdrawal issues, traders are vocal about it on public forums.

The regulatory backing provides genuine safety nets. FCA clients benefit from FSCS up to GBP 85,000 if the broker becomes insolvent. CySEC clients get ICF up to EUR 20,000. Client funds are held in segregated accounts across all regulated entities. The LSE-listed parent means financial distress would be visible in public filings long before it affected client funds.

If a withdrawal delays: contact support via live chat (available during market hours). If unresolved within 5 business days, escalate to the relevant regulator — FCA for UK, CySEC for EU, ASIC for Australia. The institutional backing means regulatory pressure carries real weight.

sections.heading: How to Open a Markets.com Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration takes under 5 minutes. Verification is typically within 24 hours. The process is straightforward — Markets.com has invested in a clean onboarding flow.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit markets.com and click Create Account. Enter your email, create a password, and select your country of residence. You will be automatically assigned to the correct regulatory entity (FCA, CySEC, ASIC, FSCA, or BVI FSC) based on location.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload government-issued ID (passport or driving licence) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months). Complete the appropriateness questionnaire required by regulators. Approval typically within 24 hours.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit $100+ via card, e-wallet, or bank transfer — all fee-free. Place a small trade. Request a withdrawal immediately — test the pipeline. If it processes within 3 business days with zero fees deducted, scale up confidently.

sections.practical_note: UK traders: select the Spread Betting account type during registration if you want tax-free profits. You can run both a CFD account and a spread betting account simultaneously. Islamic account requires a separate request after standard account approval.

sections.heading: Markets.com Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores Markets.com 7.8 out of 10. The combination of three Tier-1 regulators (FCA, CySEC, ASIC), a London Stock Exchange-listed parent company (Playtech PLC), 2,200+ CFD instruments, zero commission, and zero deposit/withdrawal fees creates a genuinely compelling proposition for the trader who values safety and simplicity above all else.

The regulatory depth here is serious. FSCS protection up to GBP 85,000 for UK clients. ICF up to EUR 20,000 for EU clients. Client funds segregated across all entities. Public financial filings through the LSE listing. This is not a broker that is going to disappear overnight with your money. The institutional infrastructure exists precisely to prevent that scenario.

The trade-off is pricing. Spread-only at 1.2+ pips EUR/USD means you pay approximately $12 per standard lot — nearly double what ECN brokers charge. The 85.4% retail loss rate tells you that this pricing model works exceptionally well for the broker. Over thousands of trades, the spread advantage compounds in the broker's favour. Active traders will find better value elsewhere.

NAFT recommends Markets.com for intermediate traders who prioritise regulatory safety and fee simplicity over raw pricing performance. The zero-fee structure on deposits and withdrawals is genuinely best-in-class. The spread betting option gives UK traders a legitimate tax advantage. The MT4/MT5 availability means you are not locked into a proprietary ecosystem. But if you execute 20+ lots daily, the spread differential versus ECN brokers will cost you $100+ per day that you could save elsewhere.
